title: Stream-span backfill protocol for partial-object lineage and graceful truncation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a robust 'stream-span' backfill and lineage protocol to handle truncated streaming JSON objects, enable safe client-initiated backfill requests, and provide a compatibility shim for older SDKs. The goal is to ensure consumers can deterministically reconstruct partial objects from arbitrarily truncated streams and request minimal replays without causing duplicate side-effects for tool/function calls.
background: We frequently see truncated structured JSON streams across network boundaries or server-side token limits. Existing heuristics (ndjson fallback, heuristic repairs) lead to brittle client-side logic and duplicate tool invocations. This ticket proposes an explicit stream-span protocol: each logical object emitted in a stream has an opaque lineage id and span metadata (span_index, total_spans optional), plus an idempotency token for any function/tool calls embedded. The client can request a backfill for a specific span range; the server will honor backfill when available or provide a compact delta if it can cheaply reconstruct missing fields.
proposal: Introduce three additions to the streaming API: (1) span markers embedded as control frames (S-START, S-CHUNK, S-END) with fields: lineage_id, span_index, total_spans (if known), fragment_checksum, and idempotency_token; (2) a backfill handshake endpoint /streams/{stream_id}/backfill that accepts lineage_id and a requested span window and returns either a replay stream or a minimized patch message; (3) a compatibility shim where older SDKs receive sentinel 'SPAN_HINT' ndjson lines that encode lineage and minimal recovery instructions.
design_decisions:
- Use opaque UUID v4 for lineage_id to avoid exposing internal model sequence numbers.
- Support both full-span replays and "delta patches" to reduce cost for large streams.
- Keep control frames lightweight (max 512 bytes) and place them outside JSON object payloads (SSE comment-style or top-level framed messages) to avoid breaking strict JSON parsers.
- Backfill is advisory: servers may refuse backfill for ephemeral or non-deterministic outputs; response must include refusal_reason.
- All tool/function calls embedded in a span must carry an idempotency_token. Backfilled spans re-emit tool call results under the same idempotency_token to allow clients to dedupe side-effects.
implementation_plan:
1) Define protocol RFC doc and proto/json schema -> Confluence (RFC link below).
2) Runtime: implement span marker emission in the serving runtime for streaming generation pass. Add a small control-frame encoder that wraps generated chunks with span metadata.
3) API: add backfill endpoint and controllers; wire to storage layer where we persist recent stream fragments for a retention window (configurable).
4) SDK: add Span-aware stream parser for JS and Python; implement compatibility shim that converts SPAN_HINT lines into span objects for older clients.
5) Tests + e2e harness: augment the streaming test harness with network truncation simulators and partial replay tests.
6) Incremental rollout: enable behind a feature flag for 10% of prod traffic, monitor correctness metrics, then widen rollout.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for control-frame encoding/decoding, checksum verification, and idempotency token handling.
- Integration tests: simulate truncation at random offsets and verify client library uses lineage_id to request backfill and reconstructs complete objects.
- Tool-call safety: tests that ensure backfilled toolcall outputs have identical idempotency_token and that client dedup logic prevents replaying side-effects.
- Load test: measure additional latency/cost for maintaining short-term fragment storage and serving backfill for common span sizes (1-8 spans).
- Compatibility tests: older SDKs receive SPAN_HINTs and can fall back to ndjson reassembly without crashing.
- Chaos tests: kill runtime mid-backfill to validate graceful refusal flows and client fallbacks.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 0: RFC + dark-launch control frame emission in staging.
- Phase 1 (FF): enable span markers and backfill endpoint for a small internal subset; retain fragments for 5 minutes.
- Phase 2: enable SDK parser updates in canary and provide polyfill for older SDKs (SPAN_HINT).
- Phase 3: increase to 50% traffic, extend retention to 30 minutes, gather metrics.
- Phase 4: GA and document in API changelog; deprecate SPAN_HINT after 3 months if adoption is high.
acceptance_criteria:
- Clients can reconstruct truncated JSON objects without manual heuristic repairs in >= 99% of simulated truncation cases.
- No duplicate side-effecting function/tool executions observed in backfill flows for idempotent-tokened calls.
- Backfill endpoint offers both replay and delta-patch modes and returns clear refusal_reason when not possible.
- SDKs successfully parse new control frames; older SDKs gracefully fall back on SPAN_HINT lines.
- Observability: traces show span lineage ids and backfill latency; dashboards added to console; alert if backfill failure rate > 2%.
risks:
- Storage overhead for fragment retention increases cost; mitigate with short retention and configurable per-customer policies.
- Non-deterministic model outputs may make faithful backfill impossible; need clear server-side refusal and client fallbacks.
- Increased complexity in streaming stack may introduce regression in throughput; require kernel-level perf tests.
- Client libraries must adopt idempotency token patterns to prevent duplicate side-effects; rollout coordination required with SDK/Docs/Support.
